records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: An internal dispatch reconciliation tool for mismatched references. Operators compared an overnight spreadsheet against a daily export; the tool surfaced understandable exceptions and warnings, with empty rows kept visible. Ada personally built the Python parser and SQL checks, gathered requirements from warehouse supervisors, and explained validation failures. Supervisors made final dispatch decisions.

decisions.reason: The name, professional description, and listed denials are supported by the transcript.
The role, employer, dates, project work, coworker training, and handbook are supported; the linked skills and achievements are also grounded in the transcript.

The source says supervisors wanted understandable exceptions and operators preferred a visible warning when a file arrived late. It does not establish that Dispatch Loom actually surfaced those warnings or exceptions as completed functionality; the summary converts preferences into implemented tool.
The transcript gives the 5-to-2-hours-per-week reconciliation measurement over six runs, identifies it as a team result, and distinguishes Ada’s contribution from coworkers’ changed habits.
The training count, two workshops, handbook, and absence of exact workshop dates are supported.
The transcript states that Ada wrote the Python parser herself.
The transcript states that Ada wrote the SQL checks herself.
The transcript states that PostgreSQL was used for the production database.
The transcript states that Git was used for version control.
The transcript supports training dispatch coworkers and writing the handbook; the category is consistent with the stated collaboration skill category.
The degree, field, institution, and dates are stated directly.
The transcript supports the certificate and date, and clarifies that it was a course completion rather than a professional license.
